ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl:
Let
F(q) := product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = product_{s in I} ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)).
We interpret [q^j] in the formal power series ring Z[[q]]. This is legitimate because every s in I satisfies s >= a+1 >= 1.

For each s in I,
(1 - q^s)^(-1) = sum_{m>=0} q^(ms)
in Z[[q]], since multiplying the right-hand side by 1 - q^s gives 1. Hence
product_{s in I} (1 - q^s)^(-1) = product_{s in I} sum_{m_s>=0} q^(m_s s).
Because I is finite, expanding this finite product gives
product_{s in I} (1 - q^s)^(-1) = sum_{(m_s)_{s in I}} q^(sum_{s in I} m_s s),
where the sum runs over all tuples of nonnegative integers (m_s) indexed by I.

Likewise,
product_{s in I} (1 - q^(r+s))
= sum_{S subseteq I} product_{s in S} (-q^(r+s))
= sum_{S subseteq I} (-1)^{|S|} q^(sum_{s in S} (r+s)).

Multiplying the two expansions, we obtain in Z[[q]]
F(q) = sum_{S subseteq I} sum_{(m_s)_{s in I}} (-1)^{|S|} q^( sum_{s in S}(r+s) + sum_{s in I} m_s s ).

Now fix j >= 0. Only finitely many terms on the right can contribute to the coefficient of q^j: the set I is finite, and if sum_{s in I} m_s s <= j then for each s in I we have 0 <= m_s <= j/s. Therefore we may read off the coefficient term-by-term:
[q^j] F(q) = sum_{S subseteq I} (-1)^{|S|} * #{ (m_s)_{s in I} : sum_{s in I} m_s s + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j }.

For each fixed S, such tuples (m_s) are in bijection with finite multisets lambda of elements of I: m_s is the multiplicity of s in lambda. Under this bijection,
wt(lambda) = sum_{s in I} m_s s.
Therefore
#{ (m_s)_{s in I} : sum_{s in I} m_s s + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j }
= #{ lambda : wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j }.
Substituting this into the previous formula gives
[q^j] F(q) = sum_{S subseteq I} sum_{lambda : wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j} (-1)^{|S|}.
But by definition, the pairs (S, lambda) appearing in this double sum are exactly the elements of X_j. Hence
[q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|},
as required.

payload.statement_nl:
Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and j >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. Define X_j to be the set of all pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, and wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j, where wt(lambda) denotes the sum of the elements of lambda. Then
[q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|},
where |S| is the cardinality of S.

dependency_assessment.notes: No external lemma/theorem citations were invoked; the argument uses only direct formal power series manipulations and a combinatorial bijection.

detailed_findings.finding: The denominator factors are correctly inverted in Z[[q]] using geometric series, valid because each s in I is positive.
The proof explicitly justifies coefficient extraction at q^j by bounding each multiplicity m_s via m_s <= j/s, so only finitely many terms contribute.
The bijection between multiplicity tuples (m_s) and finite multisets lambda of I is correct and matches the stated weight function wt(lambda).

result_payload.reason: The proof gives the standard and correct formal-power-series expansion of the product, justifies coefficient extraction for a fixed j by showing only finitely many tuples can contribute, and then identifies the contributing tuples with finite multisets of I. This yields exactly the claimed signed enumeration over X_j. It matches the lemma sketch and role in the assembly, and it does not rely on any undeclared or forbidden dependency.
